title: SYSK Selects: How the U.S. Postal Service Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun chosen by Josh, framed around the U.S. Postal Service's financial trouble and threat of Saturday delivery cuts. The hosts cover USPS finances (losses, the 2006 mandate to prefund retiree benefits, the Saturday delivery plan and its legal loophole), the history of colonial and early American mail (1639 Boston tavern drop, William Penn's post office, Thomas Neil's grant, Ben Franklin as first Postmaster General), the California gold rush mail routes, the Overland Mail Company versus the Pony Express, the 1971 reform creating the USPS, workplace shootings and the term "going postal", ZIP codes and the automated mail sorting process, postage and media mail, package competition with UPS and FedEx, PO boxes and mailbox rules, future plans like federal email addresses and clothing line, the Postal Service creed, and listener mail correcting the subliminal-message claim.

entities.name: Do We Really Want to Live Without the Post Office?

segments.title: Selects intro by Josh
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects pick, saying the Postal Service is threatened with closure and he hopes listeners will be inspired to help save it. The hosts start the show with banter.

segments.title: USPS financial crisis and Saturday delivery
segments.summary: The hosts describe USPS losses (about sixteen billion last year, five billion the year before), noting that eleven billion came from required prepayment of future retiree benefits under a 2006 law. They discuss the plan to cut Saturday delivery, the USPS argument that the stop-gap budget lacks its Saturday mandate, and the continued Saturday delivery of packages and medicine. Revenue from packages has grown while first-class mail has declined.

segments.title: Early colonial mail and postmasters
segments.summary: The hosts cover mail volume and employee counts, then early postal history: the 1639 official mail drop at Richard Fairbank's tavern in Boston, William Penn's post office in Pennsylvania, Thomas Neil's British Crown grant, and the 1774 colonial constitutional post office with Ben Franklin as first Postmaster General.

segments.title: Gold Rush mail routes and the Pony Express
segments.summary: During the California gold rush, mail went by steamship around Florida and Panama, taking three to four weeks. Overland stagecoach routes followed, with the Overland Mail Company taking about twenty-five days on the southern route. The Pony Express, run by a rival that proved the central route could run year round, averaged about ten miles an hour with riders changing horses, and was shut down after the telegraph line was completed. The hosts note Buffalo Bill Cody's disputed link to the service.

segments.title: 1971 postal reform and rural delivery
segments.summary: Mail volume boomed after the war, overwhelming the manual postal system, which led to the 1971 postal reform creating the United States Postal Service as an independent establishment. The mandate to serve every address is discussed, including the Grand Canyon donkey mail route.

segments.title: Workplace shootings and going postal
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a series of workplace shootings by postal workers beginning in the 1980s, which gave rise to the phrase 'going postal'. They mention a documentary, Murdered by Proxy, and note that retail has a higher homicide rate than the post office.

segments.title: ZIP codes and automated mail sorting
segments.summary: ZIP codes were introduced in 1963 and made mandatory in 1967, which allowed automation. The hosts explain the digits of a ZIP code and the ZIP+4 extension. They walk through a letter's journey: collection, postmarking and cancellation, barcode printing, optical address reading, sorting by carrier route, and delivery to the post office.

segments.title: Addressing envelopes, media mail, and package competition
segments.summary: The hosts cover envelope addressing guidelines such as return address placement and avoiding periods. They discuss Media Mail for books and DVDs and how Amazon shipping works. They explain that the USPS lacks a monopoly on packages, competes with UPS and FedEx, and partners with them for last-mile delivery and air transport, along with the failed 1993 submarine-launched guided missile mail test.

segments.title: Postal rates, mailboxes, and PO boxes
segments.summary: The hosts explain that changing postal rates is a lengthy bureaucratic process. They discuss mailbox placement rules set by the post office and the use of PO boxes for privacy or for avoiding forwarding.

segments.title: Future plans, postal creed, and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts discuss future USPS plans including package and prescription delivery, a clothing line, a proposed federal email address system, and a digital lock box. They discuss the 'neither rain nor snow' creed, which is linked to Herodotus, and the postal food drive. A listener correction about subliminal message speed in 1950s films (James Vicary) is read, and the episode ends with show credits.
